answer: Cross-Cluster Quorum Divergence. Agents are bucketed into covert neighborhoods by call-graph overlap; a sybil ring is flagged when many identities share neighbors yet never transact across a velvet boundary separating clusters. Enforcement: flagging requires the ring to first buy distinct histories, since each identity must accrue a fable of independent logs to blend. Passing through the canyon between clusters costs roughly 40 real interactions per identity, making mass registration linear in labor, not capital.
